correctness.rationale: For \(p=1\), \(I+\lambda D_1^{\mathsf T}D_1\) is an irreducible nonsingular M-matrix; its inverse is strictly positive, and annihilation of constants gives unit row sums, hence strict convex-combination range preservation. For \(p\ge2\) at \(n=p+1\), \(D_p\) is one binomial row \(d\) and Sherman--Morrison gives \(S=I-\alpha d^{\mathsf T}d\), \(\alpha=\lambda/(1+\lambda\binom{2p}{p})\). Applying it to the final unit vector makes coordinate \(p-2\) equal \(-\alpha\binom p2<0\). Adding a sufficiently small positive affine sequence preserves this negative output because \(D_p\) annihilates affine data. The finite verifier was read and is consistent with, but not needed for, this analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality passes for the all-order range-preservation dichotomy. The author-uploaded full text of Yamada--Tuj Jahra was read: it derives order-one smoother weights and records unit row sums, while the order-two/HP literature supplies exact weights and known sign-changing phenomena. Neither source states that order one is the unique universally range-preserving difference order or gives the uniform minimal-length counterexample for every higher order. Fresh Resultary search returned no implication-equivalent theorem.
residual_risks: An older positivity-preserving graduation or linear-smoother paper could state the same all-order dichotomy under different terminology; no such source was found.

value.rationale: Universal range preservation is a natural qualitative safety property of a linear smoother. The theorem gives a sharp all-order boundary, a minimal-sample obstruction for every higher order, and a robust strictly increasing positive witness; this is more informative than isolated negative HP weights and can guide whether unconstrained smoothing can overshoot.
residual_risks: The theorem is restricted to identity fidelity weights, uniform grids and ordinary forward differences.

limitations: Publication preparation was incomplete in the original submission; this is an administrative limitation, not a mathematical verdict.
